next_step: closed-lost — monitor for budget reset Q4-2026; re-open if migration off hyperscaler begins
notes:
POC scope: product search embeddings + chat-based support; goal to reduce average handle time for CS and rerank product results. Engaged July 2025 via trial. Procurement ramped in Nov 2025. Security team ran architecture review; asked for KMS/HSM + retention controls.

What happened:
- Strong AE/SE motion (Jordan + Maya) — multiple demos, benchmarked latency on g4 vs g5 pools.
- Engineering liked Redwood's batching and KV caching; estimated token cost looked competitive for steady-state.
- CIO and procurement favored vendor consolidation. In Jan 2026 Aurora signed with AWS Bedrock managed endpoints citing existing enterprise discount/credits and simpler billing.
- Lost champion: lead infra engineer (Naveen Rao) left Dec 2025 — no internal owner to keep the Redwood path moving.
- Pricing: Redwood offered Dedicated pricing + migration support, but couldn't match hyperscaler's year-1 bundled discounts.

Key quote: "Fits our vendor consolidation plan and lowers ops overhead in year one" — Aurora CIO (decision rationale).

Outcome: Closed-lost to AWS Bedrock (managed endpoints). Security blockers mitigated but timeline + budget favored hyperscaler. Recommend: archive and set re-engage trigger for Q4-2026 or if we see signals of multi-cloud/migration initiatives.
